blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Congestion at major Asian container ports could take several more months to ease and may persist into 2027, with vessel delays already tying up a significant share of global shipping capacity, according to a maritime industry analysis. Sea-Intelligence, a container shipping research and data firm, estimates that delays are currently absorbing 8.5% of the global container ship fleet, equivalent to about 3 million twenty-foot equivalent units, or TEUs, of capacity. Sam Chambers, a maritime analyst and editorial director of Asia Shipping Media, said that amount is “effectively removing a fleet larger than all but four global carriers from […]...
